title: Launch Mission Control — Daily Checkbook & KPI Run
content:
Purpose:
This is a working daily "mission control" checkbook for product ops to run the first 14 days of a launch (beta -> staged ramp -> open). It's designed to be light, repeatable, and actionable for the cross-functional commander on duty. Use this doc to drive the daily cadence, reconcile KPIs, and surface decisions for escalation or rollback.

How to use:
- Owner-of-the-day runs the 09:00 and 15:00 syncs, fills the KPI snapshot, and updates the 'action lane' items.
- SRE and Infra provide latency/cost deltas at each sync. Product success owns adoption metrics. Support triages incoming issues into severity lanes.
- This is intentionally terse — link to deeper artifacts for long-form analysis.

Daily cadence (example):
09:00 — Morning snapshot (15-20 min):
  - Quick state: Green/Yellow/Red for latency, errors, onboarding flow.
  - KPI snapshot: tokens/sec, median p99 latency (ms), error rate %, user growth %, daily active cohort (DAU) for new cohort.
  - Immediate blockers and one-line owner action.

12:00 — Midday health ping (async):
  - Automated dashboard check + Slack bot summary (infra).
  - If any gate trips -> page commander.

15:00 — Afternoon triage & operator handoff (30 min):
  - Review 09:00 actions, close low-effort tasks, escalate unresolved items.
  - Confirm next 24h priorities and on-call rotation.

21:00 — Nightly snapshot (optional, for high-traffic launches):
  - Incident check, capacity buffer, and routing health.

Launch traffic gates (quick pass/fail checks):
- Gate 1 (Ingress sanity): 95th percentile request success >= 99.5%; if < 99.0% then immediate rollback gate.
- Gate 2 (Latency SLO): p95 < 180ms for interactive endpoints OR explicit business exception noted.
- Gate 3 (Cost velocity): projected cost delta (24h forecast) < 3x baseline for pilot cohort.
- Gate 4 (Quality signals): automated eval failure rate < 2% on daily test prompts.
- Gate 5 (Support load): incoming tickets per 1k new users < 5; otherwise trigger product triage.

KPI snapshot template (copy into each daily update):
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner: name
- Active channel: hosted / dedicated / private
- Traffic: new users (24h), total requests (24h), peak RPS
- Cost: estimated $/24h, token-rate cost delta vs baseline
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms)
- Errors: % 5xx, rate of client errors 4xx that block onboard
- Quality: eval pass rate (automated), top 3 user-reported quality issues
- Ops load: open incidents, Sev1/2 count, average time to acknowledge
- Rollout %: % of users in cohort receiving feature (if staged)

Mini KPI example (filled):
- Date: 2025-01-05
- Owner: Maya Chen
- Active channel: hosted
- Traffic: 1,200 new users; 68k requests; peak 85 RPS
- Cost: $720/24h (projected) +12% vs baseline
- Latency: p50=48ms; p95=175ms; p99=420ms
- Errors: 5xx=0.8%; client-blocking 4xx=0.6%
- Quality: eval pass 97.2%; top issues: hallucination in address parse, truncation at 1024 tokens
- Ops load: 3 open incidents (0 Sev1, 1 Sev2), MTTA=4m
- Rollout %: 40% staged cohort

Action lanes (short list — completed items moved to 'done' section):
- Fast fixes (owner — ETA): e.g., toggle feature-heuristic A to false (Dev: Diego — 1h)
- Escalations (owner — contact): e.g., model fallbacks not triggering -> page infra-oncall (SRE: Priya)
- Investigation (owner — expected update): e.g., p99 spike correlation with batch jobs (Infra: Liam — next sync)
- Customer comms (owner): e.g., PS note for affected beta customers (CS: Nora)

Rollback decision matrix (quick):
- Immediate rollback if any of: Gate 1 fails severely (< 98% success), data exfiltration suspicion, or >10% sustained error rate for 30m.
- Partial rollback (traffic throttle) if: cost > 4x forecast OR severe quality regressions for a primary flow.
- Controlled pause (no new users) if support load or onboarding funnel failures cross thresholds.

Escalation templates (use copy/paste into Slack/email):
- Subject: [MissionControl] <urgent summary> — e.g., p95 latency breach 09:15
- Body: Time: UTC, Impacted channel, Key metrics (p95/p99/error%), Recent changes, Immediate ask (page oncall / revert commit # / route traffic)

Handover checklist (for off-duty commander):
- Confirm outstanding action lanes and owners updated.
- Post final snapshot to #launch-mission-control with tag @commander-next.
- Ensure any runbooks opened are assigned and have next-check times.

Runbook links (examples to reference):
- Incident runbook: confluence:INC-rrunbook-1
- Cost surge playbook: confluence:cost-surge-ops
- Model rollback guide: github:repo/model-serving#rollback-guide

Things we don't solve here (link deeper artifacts):
- Detailed postmortems, long-run cost modeling, A/B statistical analysis (refer to linked Confluence pages).

Open questions (to be answered in the first-week retrospective):
- Is our 15:00 triage the right time for EU-heavy launches?
- Should product own the nightly 21:00 snapshot for 7-day ramp or shift to infra?
- Do we need an automated safety throttle at API-gateway level (proposal: infra prototyping)?

Appendix — quick checklist for go/no-go at each stage (beta -> staged -> open):
- Beta (10–100 users): owner identified, manual monitoring, rollback path validated, PS onboarded with FAQ
- Staged (10–40%): automated dashboards live, traffic gates enforced, cost forecast attached, support rotation staffed
- Open (100%): SLA page published, long-run cost commit, dedicated oncall escalation path verified

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the daily doc readable — avoid dumping raw charts. Link to the dashboard snapshots instead.
- Consider a small Slackbot summary that populates the KPI snapshot automatically to reduce manual entry.
- Record time spent on each action lane to feed the retrospective on ops overhead.

Status: draft checklist with concrete template. Please review and add corrections / slot owners for the first 14 days.
